newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto sparks Pakistan opposition walkout.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto sparks Pakistan opposition walkout.

text.p: Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto led an opposition walkout from the inaugural session of Pakistan's new parliament on Wednesday when President Farooq Leghari began a televised address.

Members of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) first tried to interrupt Leghari's speech to a joint session of the Senate (upper house) and National Assembly (lower house) by raising an uproar of objections, and then walked out.
The president was unruffled and continued his Urdu-language speech marking the start of the new parliamentary year.
Deputies from Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League cheered his speech by thumping desks, drowning out opposition protests.

Bhutto later told reporters the walkout was staged to lodge a protest at what she called presidential actions of corruption and nepotism and breaking a pledge never to use his contitutional powers by sacking her as prime minister in November.
